text:
Maria: Quick heads-up — thinking about a routing-policy DSL for internal API. Want opinions before I flesh out an RFC.
Dan: Quick question: do we keep the policy canonical as a protobuf (typed) or as a JSON blob for runtime?
Oliver: Proto for validation/versioning. JSON for runtime tweaks. Both have tradeoffs.
Tara: Console POV: JSON is easier to edit and preview. We need per-route effective policy shown.
Maria: Tradeoffs: strict schema + compile-time safety (proto) vs runtime configurability (JSON). Also quota propagation and telemetry matter.
Dan: If we store canonical proto, we can serve via config-service (xDS). Console would need a conversion layer to present friendly JSON.
Oliver: gRPC clients map to proto naturally. REST clients already operate on JSON so they'd get an extra translation.
Tara: What if canonical = proto v1, but console edits are JSON that we validate/convert on save? Risk of mismatch on partial edits.
Maria: Sketch: keep proto as canonical, but mark an "editable" allowlist for console-modifiable fields. The runtime reads proto.
Dan: How do we handle quota header propagation? We still need edge proxies to forward tenant headers and policy tags.
Oliver: Edge shim today strips unknown headers. We need a whitelist for X-RW-Policy / X-Tenant and a migration plan.
DeployBot: deploy-service: canary rollout started for config-service v2 — group=platform-canary :rocket:
Tara: Canary will verify header passthrough. Also we need a telemetry signal for "policy applied" vs fallback.
Maria: Telemetry idea: emit lightweight event 'policy.evaluated' with route_id, policy_hash, outcome. Sample log:
```
policy.evaluated route_id=ingest-graphql outcome=matched policy_hash=abc123
```
Dan: That line is great — low-cardinality keys only. Avoid huge payloads.
Oliver: Tracing cost is a concern. I'd prefer counters + sampled traces when fallback happens.
Maria: Agreed: keep a counter metric for matched/denied/fallback + sample traces on fallback or mismatch.
Tara: Console wants panels: per-route quota consumed, denied, fallback-rate, and recent policy_hash.
Dan: We'll need an ETL mapping from metrics to console dashboards. Might be a new ingestion mapping job.
Maria: UX question: canary UX — percent of traffic vs tenant list? For multi-tenant safety, tenant-targeted rollout seems safer.
Tara: Support both. Percent for infra teams, tenant lists for customer-facing rollouts. Console should offer quick preview showing expected impacted tenants.
Oliver: Runtime detail: router needs weighted routing by policy-tag; current runtime can do weighted routing but we'll add tag matching.
Dan: Migration: document header rename too. Suggest rename X-Route-Policy -> X-RW-Policy to avoid collisions with external clients.
Maria: Action items: (1) draft RFC outlining proto canonical + JSON-edit flow + allowlist (2) telemetry spec for policy.evaluated and counters (3) console mock for policy editor + canary UX (4) migration checklist for oncall/edge teams.
Tara: I'll take the console mock and canary UX copy.
Oliver: I can prototype the router tag matching and header whitelist changes.
Dan: I'll own the telemetry spec and ETL mapping for dashboard panels.
Maria: I'll draft the RFC and the migration checklist. Posting a stub tomorrow morning.
Tara: One small ask: include an example policy snippet in the RFC for both proto and JSON views so PMs can review.
Maria: Will do. Also thinking versioning: reserve an extension field in the proto for future operators.
Oliver: Good call. Keep v2 compatibility in mind.
Dan: Small follow-up: when console converts JSON->proto on save, run dry-run against runtime validator and surface errors inline.
Maria: Yep — validate on save, reject if disallowed edits. We'll also surface a preview diff.
Tara: :thumbsup: Sounds good.
Maria: Thanks all — RFC stub tomorrow. I'll tag you when posted.
Dan: Thanks.
Oliver: Thanks.
DeployBot: deploy-service: canary rollout completed for config-service v2 — status=healthy
